content:
**issue-535 cold review: the narrowing was wrong, and the test I deleted was catching more than I measured**

**Two independent cold reviewers, run in parallel on #556 in separate git worktrees, converged on the same blocker with different mutations.** Recording it because the mistake is reusable, not because the fix is interesting.

**What I did.** Landing the #535 chain on `main` turned the suite red on Requirement 6's blanket ban ("no non-test module imports `governance/run-check.mjs`"), because #546 (#340) had merged in the meantime and makes `brain-check.mjs` import `runCheck` on purpose. I replaced the blanket ban with a REACHABILITY computation: derive the CI-invoked entry points from `.github/workflows`, walk their import closures through `workflow-auth`'s own `importClosure`, assert none reaches `run-check.mjs`. It looked strictly better — mechanically derived, no allowlist, reusing the guard's own machinery rather than a second copy — and it passed a live red-proof (a static import injected into `actor-check.mjs`, a real workflow entry point, went red).

**What both reviewers proved, independently.** The reachability form under-approximates at three separate places, and every under-approximation resolves toward "fine":

1. `importClosure` prunes AT `vcs/ci-context.mjs` (the D1 cut vertex) without walking its imports. Reviewer A injected `ci-context.mjs -> ci-context-helper.mjs -> run-check.mjs`; reviewer B injected `ci-context.mjs -> gitlab-api.mjs -> run-check.mjs` (an import that already exists). Full suite GREEN in both cases. Four workflow entry points carry `ci-context.mjs` in their closure, so all four would genuinely reach the multiplexer with the invariant green. **The canary I wrote for exactly this hole — "`ci-context.mjs` does not import `run-check.mjs`" — covers one arc of it, not the hole**, and my header claimed it closed the hole. That claim was false.
2. The extraction reads `.github/workflows` only. This repo ALSO ships `brain/scripts/ci/gitlab-governance.yml`, which invokes the same seven entry points with `script:` lists (ADR-0018, dogfooded, and the surface #130 depends on). Never scanned, and `runScript` only recognizes `run:` so it could not have parsed it anyway. My docstring said "every entry point every workflow in the repo invokes" — false as written.
3. `entryPoints` resolves `node <path>.mjs` and `npm run <verb>`, nothing else — not `npm test` (already used at `governance.yml:123`), not `bash wrapper.sh` (the repo's own `npm run env:init` idiom), not `npx`, not a quoted path. Each unrecognised spelling made the invariant agree with anything on that route. My red-proof used the ONE spelling the extractor handles: `red-proof-blind-along-an-unvaried-axis`, where the unvaried axis was in the EXTRACTOR, not in the assertion.

**The decisive measurement**: reviewer A re-implemented the deleted blanket predicate against the mutated tree and it flagged the offender. The test I removed caught the case my replacement missed. A narrowing justified as "keeping the property while dropping the over-approximation" had in fact dropped a chunk of the property.

**What replaced it.** Back to the blanket source-text ban — no cut vertex, no YAML parsing, no spelling dependence — plus ONE frozen exception (`brain-check.mjs`), asserted by EQUALITY so a second importer and a silently-dropped one are both red. The exception is safe for exactly one reason (no CI surface invokes `brain-check`), and that reason is a fact that can change silently, so it is asserted too: a raw substring scan for `brain-check|brain:check` over every CI file across BOTH surfaces (`.github/workflows/**` and `brain/scripts/ci/**`), comments included. Deliberately over-approximating — a mention costs a false alarm and one line of thought; a missed invocation costs the invariant. The import predicate now also matches the dynamic `import()` spelling, which the original blanket test missed too. Seven mutations, each snapshot -> edit -> read back -> run -> restore -> verify clean: every case both reviewers proved green is now red, including the frozen set's other direction.

**Generalizable, and the real lesson.** A guard has a polarity, and a REFINEMENT inherits the polarity of its weakest step. Blunt-and-over-approximating fails toward a false alarm; precise-and-computed fails toward silence, because every stage that cannot resolve its input contributes a "nothing here". When the choice is between a blunt rule with a named exception and a precise rule with a derivation, prefer the blunt one unless every stage of the derivation is itself fail-closed — and the way to find out is to mutate BEHIND each stage, not in front of it. My red-proof injected the defect where the walk was looking. Both reviewers injected it where the walk stops. That is the difference between proving a test can go red and proving it observes the thing it names.

**Corrections to two earlier records in this month's file.** Records are content-addressed and immutable — an in-place edit is caught by `rebuildIndex` as tampering (verified: it refused), so these are corrections by append, not by edit.
- `rec-897af5f4dbb254b6` (the chain closure record) says "861 changed lines against a 400-line lite budget". `tierParams('lite').diffBudget` is **1000**; 400 is the `standard`-tier literal quoted in `governance.yml` and the chain's self-imposed per-PR working limit.
- The same record lists `brain-writes-reviewed` going green as real-run VCS_TOKEN evidence. It is not: the job passed on rule 1 before any port call (this PR touches no `brain/core/**` or `brain/project/**` file), and at `lite` the review fetch is skipped outright (`brain-writes-reviewed.mjs:357`). The genuine evidence is `issue-link`, which fails closed on both an uncomputable body and an `issueView` failure, so green requires two successful authenticated calls. `actor-check`'s LOG is evidence; its green alone is not (`!author -> warn -> exit 0`).
- `rec-b70d33d3d22e62d2` (my landing record) says "Non-test changed lines ~381". The measured figure is **411** (327 additions, 84 deletions, excluding the ignoreList), which is what the PR body states.

**Filed out of scope, not fixed here**: `governance-relabel.yml` carries the exact #535 defect (`GH_TOKEN` on a step whose entry point imports `getVcs`) and escapes the guard because the audited set is a hand-written three-element list; `workflow-auth` answers "nothing to report" for `node "quoted/path.mjs"`; the audit only ever reports need>declared, so over-credentialing a credential-free job is invisible, and its `permissions:` check covers `pull-requests` but not `issues: read`, which `issue-link` needs.
